heading: What the game is
snippet: Grump the Baby Destroyer  is a browser-based 3D survival-horror game. You play a baby left behind in an empty school. Runs entirely in the browser — no build step, no backend, no install — and multiplayer is peer-to-peer

snippet: Bob is the danger of the night, from night 1 onward, on every difficulty. He is never shown on the map (see  The Map ).

snippet: Patrol.  Wanders the halls, sweeping a torch and humming. Speed  1.5 + min(0.7, (night−1)×0.12) . From night 2, 45% of the time he heads for a lit room instead of a random hall corner (if the generator is running) — and

snippet: Grump starts every run as a boy in green dungarees who wants to talk. He becomes "the thing the game is named after" once he "turns" — on  day 4  at the latest, or earlier if his resentment meter hits 100 first.

heading: The design rule
snippet: There is no correct answer. Every option costs resentment — some less than others, but never zero — and refusing to talk to him at all costs the most of all:  +6 resentment at the following nightfall  if you never spoke

heading: How a question is picked
snippet: When you talk to Grump, the game first works out his current tier from his resentment total, then picks a random question from that tier that you haven't been asked yet this run (falling back to any question at or below

heading: Every question, in order of tier
snippet: Cost is shown as resentment added if you pick that answer.

heading: Calm (resentment 0–21)
snippet:
Hallo. Are you having a nice last day? 
  −6  “Yes! Very nice!”  Nice. Everyone had a nice one. I asked you about YOURS.  
  −5  “Not really.”  Then you should have gone home. Like the others did.  
  −8  “...”  Silence.

heading: Uneasy (22–49)
snippet:
Why did they all get picked up and you did not? 
  −6  “They forgot me.”  Nobody forgets. They decide, and then they call it forgetting.  
  −8  “I do not know.”  You do know. You are just not saying it out loud yet.

heading: Cold (50–74)
snippet:
The little ones. Are you keeping them from me? 
  −10  “They are just safe with me.”  Safe. There is that word again.  
  −12  “No.”  I counted them yesterday. I count very well.  
  −9  “Yes.”  At last. Something true.

heading: Hostile (75+)
snippet:
How many nights do you think you get? 
  −14  “As many as I need.”  Need. Listen to it. NEED.  
  −12  “I do not know.”  I do. I have the number. I am not telling you the number.  
  −16  “Enough to get out.”  Out. There

snippet:

heading: What stays local
snippet: The Pokémon-card boy (the Card Kid) and his encounter with the Taker are deliberately  not  networked — everybody who triggers it gets their own private version, on their own screen, invisible to teammates. See  Characte

heading: Chat
snippet: Press  T  to open a chat line (co-op only), type your message, and press Enter to send it to the group.

heading: What is never shown
snippet:
Bob never appears on the map, at any time, under any circumstances.  You have no way to see him coming except your own eyes and ears. 
    Grump only appears while it's daytime and before he has turned.  At night, or fro

heading: Rooms lit on the map
snippet: While the generator is running, every currently-lit non-hallway room is tinted faintly amber on the map, so you can tell at a glance which rooms Bob has already switched off behind him.

heading: Tips & Strategy
snippet:
Tips & Strategy 
 Every tip here follows directly from a mechanic documented elsewhere on this wiki — see the linked pages for the underlying numbers.

heading: Keep the generator boring
snippet: Repair before you refuel.  Condition below 30% risks a random stall at any moment, and wear itself adds up to 0.12/s to the burn rate — a generator at 50% condition burns noticeably faster than one at 100%, on top of eve

heading: Beating Bob
snippet: A lit room is a full stop, but only if you're not already caught.  He gives up chasing the instant you reach one (unless he's standing right next to you) — so knowing where the nearest lit room is matters more than pure

heading: Managing Grump
snippet:
Say something, anything, every day.  Not talking to him at all costs +6 resentment at nightfall — more than most single answers. There is no way to avoid paying him some attention.

heading: General survival
snippet:
Eat before you're desperate.  Below 20% food you move slower, and below 15% your fear rises faster too — hunger compounds every other problem at once.

snippet:
Room codes are five letters, generated by  PeerJS  when the host opens a room. A few things to check:

heading: Why do my searches keep coming up empty?
snippet: This is by design and gets more noticeable the longer a run goes: the odds of a container actually holding something drop every night, hitting their leanest around night 8 and staying there. See  Loot Tables  for the exa

heading: Grump turned before day 4 — is that a bug?
snippet: No. Pushing his resentment to 100 through rude answers, ignoring him, or leaving messes uncleaned brings his turn forward; being polite never delays it past day 4. Day 4 is a hard ceiling, not a fixed trigger point — see

heading: I can't find Bob on the map
snippet: That's intentional — Bob is never shown on the map, at any time, in any circumstance. See  The Map .

heading: I lost the game / it crashed — is progress saved?
